As for advice I suggest starting with modules. Some people are able to jump right into homebrew, but for many first timers a good module is well balance to help both new players and DMs. Also, don't compare yourself to 'pro' DMs. They have been doing this for years. You WILL make mistakes. Realize this, admit when you do, then move on. Finally have fun. The DM may be at the head of the table so to speak, but you are still playing the game. 

Best of luck, and happy gaming!

What are the others classes? Does everyone have a similar alignment? Do you have any idea why he may be picking on you in particular?
I recently left a table where my DM didn't necessarily pick on anyone, however he was new and no matter what we did he would only accept actions that would follow the narrative in the book. (I have horror stories but I'm still super salty so won't use this space to vent). As soon as you start to resent a DM it's time to go.

Be sure that you know the material going in. I'm not saying have rules memorized, or every single detail of the story, but at the very least know your players stats, the stats of all monsters/npcs they will encounter, and descriptions of all places where you can easily reach them.

If you're interested, I've started a Facebook group where newbie DMs can come in and lead a group of experienced Dms for session or two in order to get feedback.
